answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by weighing identities through the shape of their interaction graph, not just their count. Each agent's standing grows only from attestations by peers outside its own cluster, so a farm of fake identities that mostly vouch for each other forms a tight trellis of mutual praise that the network discounts as hollow, while a cipher of shared behavior across the cluster flags the whole group for review. Every added fake deepens the cluster and lowers each member's weight, so the cost of the next fake rises while its value falls.
